sources.comment: Was disabled on the live server 2026-08-25 after five dead days and three escalating quarantines; RE-ENABLED the same day 17:54 and holding (+77 polls, zero failures, no quarantine). MEASURED, so do NOT reach for timeout_seconds (ISSUE_107): the 30d journal makes it the FASTEST feed in this set — p50 410ms, p95 571ms, p99 751ms over 33,952 polls, 22 failures (99.94% success). The failures are bimodal, either ~400ms or the full deadline burnt twice at ~20.8s, which is a host stalling mid-connection rather than a slow feed; a longer deadline only waits longer for the same nothing. What held it out was the quarantine ladder through a bad stretch, and the ladder will catch it again if the stalls return.

Behind Cloudflare Bot-Management. CONFIRMED WALLED ON THE SERVER, 2026-08-25 (ISSUE_107): feed_doctor there returns 403 with the Cloudflare interstitial ("Just a moment...") — the JS browser challenge no feed reader can pass. A dev-container probe the same day returned 200 with 10 entries; that was the DEV egress, not the engine's, and taking it as recovery would have been exactly the mistake CLAUDE.md warns about. Re-enable only after feed_doctor_cli ON THE SERVER answers 200.

Replaces theblock's tier (ISSUE_107) — established, editorially independent crypto desk. Probed 2026-08-25: 200, 12 entries, newest 1.1h; fires 0 of this set's keywords on current contents, so it enters as corroboration volume rather than as a fast-path source.

Replaces cryptoslate's tier (ISSUE_107). Probed 2026-08-25: 200, 22 entries, newest 0.1h, 1 of 22 matching this set's keywords. Independent of the four incumbents, which is what makes its duplicates count as cross-feed corroboration.

Tier B candidate (ISSUE_107) — BTC-focused desk, independent of the incumbents. Probed 2026-08-25: 200, 10 entries, newest 12.1h. Switch on only once ISSUE_106 records the detection trigger: high_cluster_size 5 was calibrated on the July feed mix and becomes a routine story once this set runs many feeds.

Tier B candidate (ISSUE_107). Probed from the dev container 2026-08-25: 200, 16 entries, newest 1.1h, 2 of 16 matching this set's keywords (a chain halt and a delisting). BUT WALLED ON THE SERVER the same day: 403 with the Cloudflare interstitial ("Just a moment..."). Not promotable on this host — kept declared so the finding is recorded rather than rediscovered.

Tier B candidate (ISSUE_107) — investigative desk whose beat IS this set's vocabulary: 3 of 10 current items match (30%, the highest of any candidate). Probed 2026-08-25: 200, newest 19.7h. Low volume, high keyword density; the pairing to watch when deciding whether keyword_source_weight discriminates at all (ISSUE_82 / ISSUE_106).

Tier B candidate (ISSUE_107) — DeFi desk, exploits and governance attacks are its beat: 10 of 100 current items match this set's keywords. Probed 2026-08-25: 200, newest 16.8h. A poll floor because 100 entries per fetch is the largest of any candidate and the fast loop pays for it every pass.

Tier B candidate (ISSUE_107). Probed 2026-08-25: 200, 30 entries, newest 0.1h. Broader than crypto — general AI and geopolitics items arrive with it, one of which matched 'collapse' on US-Canada trade talks. Cross-market bleed is worth knowing about: the article corpus is shared, so forex_news's detector counts these neighbours too (ISSUE_106).

Tier B candidate (ISSUE_107). Probed 2026-08-25: 200, 10 entries, newest 13.8h. Weighted 0.6 rather than 0.8 because bitcoinist — a working feed, deliberately NOT declared — belongs to the same publisher network: whichever of the two runs, its duplicates are intra-network and inflate cluster_size without adding an independent voice.
Tier B candidate (ISSUE_107) — recall tier. Probed 2026-08-25: 200, 20 entries, newest 0.6h, 0 keyword matches.
Tier B candidate (ISSUE_107) — recall tier. Probed 2026-08-25: 200, 10 entries, newest 0.0h, 1 of 10 matching.

Tier B candidate (ISSUE_107) — highest-volume candidate at 95 entries per fetch and predominantly price commentary ('BTC Reclaims $81K'), which is duplicate-heavy by nature. Probed 2026-08-25: 200, newest 0.9h, 3 of 95 matching. Weight 0.6 plus a 5-minute poll floor: recall without paying for it on the fast loop, and without letting it dominate the cluster-size distribution.

Tier B candidate (ISSUE_107) — the primary source for half this set's vocabulary ('SEC', 'lawsuit'), which reaches us today only through third-party reporting. Probed 2026-08-25: 200, 25 entries, newest 162h. HELD AT 0.8 DELIBERATELY: the keyword list contains the bare token 'SEC' and every SEC press-release title begins with it, so the fast-path would fire on 25 of 25 current items — 6x the busiest incumbent (cointelegraph, 16.7%). At 0.8 it feeds the corpus and the cluster path without ever self-flagging. Promoting it to 1.0 depends on ISSUE_46 narrowing 'SEC' to phrases ('SEC charges', 'SEC sues'). Publishes on a schedule, not a news cycle: observed 7d (2026-08-25) — right at the 168h default, which would flap. The 720h allowance is what both delivery checks judge it by (ISSUE_107) — without it the 168h default calls a healthy press feed STALE and SILENT.

Tier B candidate (ISSUE_107) — the derivatives-regulator twin of sec_press. Probed 2026-08-25: 200, 10 entries, newest 93.3h, 0 of 10 matching this set's keywords (its house style does not use the bare token, unlike the SEC's). Kept at the same weight as sec_press so the two regulators are one comparable tier rather than two hand-set values. Publishes on a schedule, not a news cycle: observed 4d (2026-08-25). The 720h allowance is what both delivery checks judge it by (ISSUE_107) — without it the 168h default calls a healthy press feed STALE and SILENT.

Tier B candidate (ISSUE_107) — exchange announcements, where a halt or a delisting ORIGINATES before news feeds carry it. Probed 2026-08-25: 200, 10 entries, newest 0.6h, 0 of 10 matching: the current contents are marketing ('Kraken Pro on TradingView'), so the precision argument is about the rare item, not the average one. Weight 0.6 and a poll floor until source_contribution_cli says whether the rare item is worth the average one.

Tier B candidate (ISSUE_107) — the only other exchange announcement feed that exists at all: binance answers 202 with an empty body, coinbase and bybit 403, and bitfinex, okx, gemini, gate, bitget, mexc and htx all 404. Probed 2026-08-25: 200, 50 entries, newest 2.7h, 0 matching — heavily promotional (mining campaigns, reward programmes). Lowest weight in the set and a poll floor: it is admitted for listing and delisting notices, and it is the first candidate source_contribution_cli should be asked to justify.
